narrative.text: Introduces the third WHO report on its COVID-19 response in Somalia, covering March 2020 to March 2022 and organised in line with WHO's strategic preparedness and response plan. Section 1 describes how WHO helped national and state health authorities lead the response from the first case in March 2020, using incident management support teams and leading UN coordination bodies. Later sections, based on the headings, cover building essential public health functions, rolling out COVID-19 vaccines and maintaining essential health services. The section ends with a story on infection prevention and control training and figures on treatment centres, oxygen supplies, protective equipment and kits provided with WHO support.

Describes how WHO Somalia used data, research and digital tools such as EWARN, dashboards, a community health worker app, chatbots and CommCare vaccine registration covering over 1.3 million people to guide its COVID-19 response. It reports on research studies, publications and information notes produced, which built local research capacity. The final section draws lessons for an inclusive recovery, arguing for investment in primary health care, essential public health functions and the health workforce to build resilience and progress towards universal health coverage, followed by acknowledgements of donors.

The front matter of the WHO report on its response to COVID-19 in Somalia, 2020–2022, published by the Eastern Mediterranean Regional Office, with copyright, licence, cataloguing data and ISBNs. The contents list six sections on crisis management, public health functions, vaccine roll-out, essential services, research and lessons for recovery. A foreword by the WHO Representative describes building testing, surveillance and treatment capacity in a fragile health system and names primary health care, essential public health functions and the health workforce as key areas for investment.
